hero.subtitle: Every outing becomes a memory, every observation a story to share.

features.title: Discover Naturegraph
features.subtitle: Observe and discover nature, together.
features.card1Desc: Note what you see during your outings, whether it's a species, a landscape or a memorable moment.
features.card2Desc: Publish your encounters, add photos and tell what you felt. Each outing becomes a story.
features.card3Desc: Join a caring community that shares their outings and contributes to the evolution of Naturegraph.

values.title: What guides us daily
values.item1Desc: We share our progress, our choices and our thoughts with the community. Every user can follow the project's evolution and contribute with their ideas.
values.item2Desc: Naturegraph exists thanks to its migrators. Together, we explore, share and bring nature to life through our observations and stories.
values.item3Desc: Every outing is an experience to share: photos, stories or unique moments. The richness of the project comes from what each person contributes.

cta.title: What if every outing became a story?

mission.title: Give meaning to every observation
mission.paragraph1: Nature is present everywhere, in everyday life. Naturegraph helps keep track of encounters and share discoveries.
mission.paragraph2: By combining technology and collective intelligence, Naturegraph offers a new way to explore local biodiversity.

discord.title: Join us on Discord!
discord.description: An open space to exchange, whether you are curious, passionate or just passing through.
discord.benefit1: Share your outings and discoveries with other members
discord.benefit2: Discuss observations, species and nature practices
discord.benefit3: Follow the project evolution and upcoming features

faq.title: Answers to your questions
faq.a1: Yes! Naturegraph is completely free. Later, a premium version with advanced features will support the project.
faq.q2: Do I need to be an expert to contribute?
faq.a2: Absolutely not! Naturegraph is designed for everyone, from beginner to experienced enthusiast.
faq.q3: When will the app be available?
faq.a3: The MVP will be available in early 2026 for the first registered users.
faq.q4: How can I track my observations?
faq.a4: Each user has a profile that centralizes their observations and shares.

storytelling.title: The stoat, our animal totem
storytelling.intro: Every project needs a guide. The stoat embodies the values that drive us daily.
storytelling.trait1Desc: Like the stoat that adapts to seasons by changing its coat, Naturegraph evolves with its community.
storytelling.trait2Desc: Always on the move, the stoat explores its territory with the same curiosity that drives our migrators.
storytelling.trait3Desc: The stoat observes before acting. Naturegraph respects your pace and your way of exploring nature.
storytelling.closing: The stoat reminds us that a community's strength lies in the attention paid to every detail of nature.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.section0Content:
Naturegraph is currently in a private closed beta phase, operated personally and non-commercially by Nicolas Douaron from Quebec (Canada).

In concrete terms:

• Access is restricted to people who received an explicit invitation (individual access key).
• No service level agreement (SLA) is guaranteed during this phase.
• Data collected is minimal and retained only as long as needed for the beta.
• The service may be interrupted, modified or reset at any time without notice, to improve the platform.
• Your data can be deleted at any time on simple request to naturegraph.fr@gmail.com.
• No monetization is performed during the beta: no payment, no advertising, no commercial sharing.

By joining the beta with your access key, you acknowledge having read this experimental status and accept to test the service under these conditions.
privacy.section1Content:
Naturegraph is a collaborative web platform for sharing naturalist observations (photos, species, descriptions and location).

This policy transparently explains how your personal data is collected, used and protected. It is drafted in compliance with Quebec's Law 25 and the European GDPR.
privacy.section2Content:
We only collect data necessary for the service to function:

• email address
• username (nickname)
• observation content (text, photos, species, location if enabled)
• minimal technical data (device type, anonymized technical logs)

No sensitive data is intentionally collected (health, political opinions, biometric data, etc.). EXIF metadata (GPS, capture date) is automatically removed from your photos before storage.
privacy.section3Content:
Your data is used exclusively to:

• create and manage your account
• display your observations on the platform
• improve the user experience during the beta
• ensure the security of the service

Naturegraph never sells, rents or shares your data for commercial or advertising purposes.
privacy.section4Content:
Location data is optional.

You can:
• enable it to enrich your observations
• disable it at any time in your device settings
• mask the precise location of an observation to reveal only the region ("make public" option at step 3)

Some locations may be automatically blurred to protect sensitive species (raptors, rare orchids, etc.).
privacy.section5Content:
Naturegraph uses only essential cookies:

• user session
• technical preferences (language, light/dark theme)

No advertising or marketing tracking cookies are placed. No third-party analytics tools (Google Analytics, etc.) are used.
privacy.section6Content:
• Account data: retained as long as your account is active.
• Account deletion: immediate on request from your settings or by email.
• Technical backups: may persist up to 7 to 30 days via the hosting provider's automatic rotation (Supabase) before full disappearance.
• End of beta: all data may be deleted if the decision is made not to continue the service. You will be notified by email at least 30 days in advance to export your data.
privacy.section7Content:
You have the following rights over your data at any time:

• access
• rectification
• deletion
• portability (export your data as JSON from your settings)
• opposition to processing
• withdrawal of consent

To exercise these rights, contact us at naturegraph.fr@gmail.com. We respond within a maximum of 30 days.
privacy.section8Content:
We implement the following technical measures:

• encryption of data in transit (HTTPS / TLS)
• strict access control at the database level (PostgreSQL Row Level Security)
• secure storage via Supabase
• secure account deletion (full cascade + storage cleanup)
• automatic removal of location metadata (EXIF) from photos before upload
• automatic compression and resizing of photos to limit stored data
privacy.section9Content:
Your data is processed by our technical service providers:

• Frontend: Vercel Inc. (340 S Lemon Ave #4133, Walnut, CA 91789, USA) — vercel.com
• Database and storage: Supabase Inc., AWS us-east-2 region (Ohio, USA) — supabase.com

Your data is therefore hosted in the United States. For users in the European Union, the transfer is based on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) of the European Commission, in accordance with Article 46 of the GDPR. For Quebec users, this transfer complies with the requirements of Law 25 (informed consent + equivalent protection measures).
privacy.section10Content:
Privacy contact: naturegraph.fr@gmail.com

Data controller: Nicolas Douaron, Quebec resident (Canada), operating Naturegraph in a personal capacity during the private beta phase.

No postal address is published during the private beta. For any official correspondence requiring an address, contact us first by email — we will provide the appropriate address based on the nature of your request.
privacy.section11Content:
Quebec's Law 25 (Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information) applies as a priority to users residing in Quebec.

Your rights:

• access to your personal information
• rectification
• deletion
• cessation of dissemination / de-indexing
• portability (since September 22, 2024)
• opposition to processing

To exercise these rights, contact naturegraph.fr@gmail.com.

In case of unresolved dispute, you may file a complaint with the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI) — cai.gouv.qc.ca.

terms.title: Legal Notice
terms.section0Title: ⚠️ Private beta status — personal experimental project
terms.section0Content:
Naturegraph is currently operated personally and non-commercially by Nicolas Douaron, Quebec resident (Canada), in a private closed beta phase.

No commercial legal structure (company, NEQ, SIRET) is associated with the service during this phase. Access is restricted to people who received an explicit invitation (individual access key).

The service is provided "as-is", without any guarantee of accuracy, availability or fitness for a particular purpose. Use is voluntary and experimental.

This status will be updated if Naturegraph evolves into a commercial structure (incorporation, monetization), with prior notice to users.
terms.section1Content:
Service name: Naturegraph

Description: collaborative web platform dedicated to observing and sharing biodiversity.

Publication director: Nicolas Douaron, in a personal capacity.

Operating location: Quebec (Canada).

Contact: naturegraph.fr@gmail.com

No business number is published during the private beta — the service is not commercialized. An update will occur as soon as a legal structure is potentially incorporated.
terms.section2Content:
The service is hosted by:

• Frontend (web interface): Vercel Inc., 340 S Lemon Ave #4133, Walnut, CA 91789, USA — vercel.com
• Database, storage and server functions: Supabase Inc., AWS us-east-2 region (Ohio, USA) — supabase.com

User data is hosted on US territory. See the Privacy Policy ("Hosting and international transfers" section) for the associated safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses for EU users, Law 25 compliance for Quebec users).
terms.section3Content:
All content produced by Naturegraph (interface, design, editorial texts, logo, icons, visual identity) is protected by copyright (Canada Copyright Act + French Intellectual Property Code for European users).

Users remain entirely owners of the content they publish (photos, observations, descriptions). By publishing on Naturegraph, they grant the service a non-exclusive license strictly necessary for the operation of the platform (display, storage, technical backup).

Any unauthorized reproduction of the publisher's content, or other users' content without their consent, is prohibited.
terms.section4Content:
Naturegraph provides a collaborative platform on an experimental basis.

Observations, species identifications and information shared by users are provided for informational and community purposes. Naturegraph does not guarantee the scientific accuracy, completeness or absence of errors in user-published content.

The user is solely responsible for the content they publish. They agree to respect the community charter, applicable laws (copyright, species protection, third-party privacy) and not to publish illegal, defamatory or harmful content.

Naturegraph cannot be held liable for direct or indirect damages resulting from the use of the service during the beta phase.
terms.section5Content:
The processing of personal data is covered by a dedicated privacy policy, compliant with Quebec's Law 25 and the European GDPR.

See: Privacy Policy.
terms.section6Content:
The applicable law depends on the user's place of residence:

• Quebec's Law 25 and Canadian law for residents of Quebec and Canada (primary law of the service).
• European GDPR and applicable national law for residents of the European Union.

In case of dispute, an amicable resolution will systematically be sought first via the contact naturegraph.fr@gmail.com.

Failing amicable agreement:

• Quebec residents may file with the Commission d'accès à l'information (CAI) or competent Quebec courts.
• EU residents may file with the supervisory authority of their country (CNIL in France) or competent courts in their place of residence.

Use of the service implies acceptance of these legal terms.
